evidence_class: mocked: a local durable directory backend behind a granted artifact store, fixture launch registrations, a backend wrapper that loses acknowledgements and a fake clock; no object store, worker Pod or harness was used. Live G8 qualification belongs to the integration package.
interfaces: Publisher.publish(doc, materials) refuses scope_mismatch before any upload when the manifest authority is not the granted store scope; refuses superseded_generation when a pointer of a newer task generation exists, scope_mismatch when another execution already holds a pointer of this generation, stale_sequence for a checkpoint_sequence at or below this generation's pointer, and identity_conflict when the same checkpoint id and sequence arrive with other content; otherwise it uploads every material under the immutable artifact id checkpoint_id.role, commits the manifest through Validator.commit only after every object reads back verified, checks the generation fence again, and writes one write-once pointer keyed by task generation and checkpoint_sequence
A replay of a promoted checkpoint with identical content returns promoted with reason replayed and adds nothing

Publisher.latest() reads only the newest generation that holds a pointer and returns its highest sequence whose recorded manifest matches the pointer and verifies authoritative; it never falls back to an older generation, and a stale attempt cannot verify a newer generation's manifest

Publisher.sequence() gives this generation's highest pointer sequence; Publisher.reclaim(checkpoint_id) removes the material records of a checkpoint whose manifest never committed, never a newer generation's record, and keeps any object another record names

worker.supervisor.Schedule.tick() captures and publishes when due, then stretches the next interval so capture time stays within Budget.overhead of it; a lost acknowledgement counts interrupted and the same captured checkpoint is republished under its identity on the next tick; superseded_generation stops periodic promotion

Schedule.drain() publishes off schedule under its own Budget.drain deadline and Budget.drain_attempts, refusing drain_budget_exceeded when capture overruns the deadline; Schedule.metrics() adds checkpoint_age_seconds

outcomes.observed: the three case records lifted from proofs run 38153968595 at the tested commit, each run twice in independent fixtures with equal results
outcomes.accepted: the publisher returns promoted only after Validator.commit verifies the manifest and every inventory object
outcomes.committed: a checkpoint is current only through its pointer, written after the manifest verifies
outcomes.externally_verified: none: no object store or deployed worker was exercised

rollback: Stop calling Schedule.tick and Schedule.drain to stop periodic promotion; pointers and manifests already written stay, so Publisher.latest keeps returning the last complete checkpoint. Lowering the checkpoint write_minor below 2 makes Validator.commit refuse promotion_disabled, which the publisher reports without writing a pointer.
limitations: No production caller yet: the Pod supervisor drain path and the recovery Checkpoints listing do not call the publisher; SV2-CKP-05 owns restore decisions
git_capture.checkpoint and the native checkpoint commit manifests directly and are not fenced by generation; only Publisher.publish promotes
The rollback has not been rehearsed against a deployed worker
Pointer writes rely on the backend's single object write being atomic, true for the local backend and an S3 put
